Dipyridamole (300 to 400 mg) has also been given as an oral suspension; thallium-201 is given about 45 minutes later to coincide with peak dipyrida- mole-serum concentrations. Dipyridamole has also been used in echocardiography.1,2 The in- travenous dipyridamole dose used to obtain maximum sensitivi- ty is often higher (750 to 840 micrograms/kg) than the dose used in scintigraphy.1 1. The value of long-term antiplatelet therapy with aspirin in patients who have suffered an ischaemic stroke (p.1185) or transient ischaemic attack is well-established, with a reduction in the risk of both stroke and other vascular events.1 The use of dipyridamole has been more controversial. Early studies with dipyridamole, used alone or with aspirin, failed to show any ben- efit over aspirin alone. The European Stroke Prevention Study-2 (ESPS-2),2 which compared aspirin and dipyridamole, alone or together, with placebo, found that both drugs reduced the risk of stroke and that the effects appeared to be additive.
